description: Native Solanum Umbra career talents, background generation, general talent use, and equipment requirement rules from pages 131-144.

entries.title: Career Talent System
entries.summary: Professional careers grant Minor and Major talents governed by native attributes; actions without a relevant talent are attempted at a default -4 penalty.
body: The source provides complete talent tables for Hunter, Mechanic, Medic, Scavenger, and Warlord. Each talent identifies a governing statistic and a specific capability.

When an action involves a possessed professional talent, the GM applies the relevant talent bonus or benefit. When no relevant talent or specialized training applies, the action is performed at a default -4 penalty.

Trader appears in the earlier career list, but no Trader Minor or Major Talent table appears in this chapter or elsewhere in the manuscript search. The wiki records that omission rather than creating replacement talents.

tables.title: Hunter Minor Talents
rows: Move quietly, avoid detection, and aid others with stealth checks
Set up and disarm basic traps; craft improvised traps from raw materials
Read natural signs and maps; navigation and map-reading checks at +5
Automatically pass Difficulty 15 survival checks or lower
Improved ranged accuracy; reroll one failed shot per session
Attempt to train and control wild animals
Blend into natural surroundings and attempt natural-environment disguise

tables.title: Hunter Major Talents
rows: Track targets across long distances and complex terrain
Survive extreme conditions and improvise solutions
Long-range precision; reroll ranged damage once per session
Anticipate enemy actions; anticipated enemy action suffers -1
Communicate and form bonds with wild creatures

tables.title: Mechanic Minor Talents
rows: Work with electrical systems and wiring
Efficiently extract useful parts from junk
Expertise with a wide variety of tools

tables.title: Mechanic Major Talents
rows: Deep understanding of complex machinery and systems
Design and build weaponry and defenses
Combine multiple technological systems into functional units
Quickly learn and adapt to new technologies
Perform high-stakes repairs and modifications in the field

tables.title: Medic Minor Talents
rows: Use medicinal plants and natural treatments
Identify symptoms and causes of illness
Handle severe injuries and high-stress treatment

tables.title: Medic Major Talents
rows: Use advanced surgery in harsh conditions
Develop new medical treatments and technologies
Treat severe trauma and stabilize critical patients

tables.title: Scavenger Minor Talents
rows: Find food and useful materials in the wild
Quickly repair and adapt items using found materials

tables.title: Scavenger Major Talents
rows: Create advanced devices from found materials
Access secret or rare knowledge about resources and technology

tables.title: Warlord Major Talents
rows: Lead and direct troops in combat
Develop and execute complex war strategies
Master warfare across psychological and tactical dimensions

sourceRefs.notes: Five complete career talent families; Trader remains listed elsewhere but lacks a talent table.

entries.title: In-Depth Character Background Generation
entries.summary: Six 1d20 tables generate upbringing, key life events, relationships, motivations, fears or flaws, and significant possessions.
body: The background generator is optional and intended to enrich history, hooks, relationships, and motivations rather than replace the earlier origin and motivation tables.
Roll once on each table or choose results that fit the intended character.

tables.title: Upbringing
rows: Makeshift family or community without biological ties
Privileged background now ruined or gone
Constant travel with a nomadic group

tables.title: Key Life Events
rows: Death or disappearance of someone close
Leadership role with mixed possible outcome

tables.title: Personal Motivations
rows: Revenge against those who wronged the character
Quest for lost knowledge or understanding

tables.title: Fears and Flaws
rows: Severe anxiety in darkness or confined spaces

entries.title: Talent Rolls and Equipment Requirements
entries.summary: The GM selects relevant attributes or professional talents; lacking relevant training imposes -4, while advanced equipment may require a profession, talent, or minimum attribute.
body: When a player attempts an action or is subjected to one, the GM determines the relevant statistic or professional talent and applies its bonus or penalty.
If no relevant talent or specialized training exists, the action suffers a default -4 penalty.
Advanced gear may require a named talent, profession, or minimum attribute. The GM may deny use, impose penalties, or allow an improvised alternative when requirements are not met.
Examples include Expert Marksman for high-tech weapons, Tech Specialist for drone maintenance, and Strength 15 for heavy melee weapons.

sourceRefs.notes: General talent resolution, -4 untrained penalty, and profession/talent/attribute equipment requirements.
